title: HfO2/SiO2 chirped Bragg stack for broadband blocking
scientific_hypothesis: A chirped period distribution in the Bragg reflector sections broadens the blocking bandwidth to cover 300-1100 nm more effectively than uniform quarter-wave stacks.
design_principle: Chirping the layer thicknesses (varying the period across the stack) creates multiple overlapping stopbands that merge into a broader blocking region. This addresses the challenge of blocking both visible and NIR with one structure.
proposed_topology: Air | HfO2(1)/SiO2(1) | HfO2(2)/SiO2(2) | HfO2(3)/SiO2(3) | HfO2(4)/SiO2(4) | HfO2(5)/SiO2(5) | HfO2_cavity | SiO2(5)/HfO2(5) | SiO2(4)/HfO2(4) | SiO2(3)/HfO2(3) | SiO2(2)/HfO2(2) | SiO2(1)/HfO2(1) | SiO2_substrate
design_variables: Individual layer thicknesses for all 11 layers (5 chirped pairs + 1 cavity + 5 chirped pairs)
soft_objectives: Achieve uniform blocking across both visible and NIR bands
manufacturing_considerations: Total layer count is 11, well under 30-layer limit
Chirped design requires precise thickness control across the stack
HfO2 and SiO2 are conventional depositable materials
theory_basis: Chirped Bragg reflector theory for broadband reflection
Transfer matrix method for non-periodic stacks
expected_advantages: Broader blocking bandwidth than uniform quarter-wave stacks
Fewer layers needed for same blocking performance
Better coverage of 300-1100 nm range with single structure
known_risks: Chirp optimization is more complex than uniform stacks
May sacrifice passband sharpness for blocking width
Thickness gradient may be harder to manufacture reproducibly
execution_request_english: Design a chirped-stack bandpass filter on fused silica substrate with air incidence. Stack: 5 chirped HfO2/SiO2 (Gao) pairs with varying thicknesses, one HfO2 cavity layer at center, then 5 chirped SiO2 (Gao)/HfO2 pairs in reverse order. Total 11 layers. Optimize individual layer thicknesses and chirp rate to maximize transmittance in 255-280 nm while minimizing transmittance in 300-700 nm and 700-1100 nm. No metal layers. Materials: hfo2, SiO2 (Gao).
